chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and Hisham ibn Salim, and Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, and others, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If the people were to neglect Hajj, it would be upon the governor to compel them to do so and to stay there; and if they were to neglect the visitation of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), it would be upon the governor to compel them to do so and to stay there. So if they do not have wealth, he should spend from the treasury of the Muslims on them.
ai.seo_question: What is the governor's role in ensuring the community performs Hajj and visits the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the political and religious authority of the Imam or governor (al-Wali) to enforce communal obligations, extending the concept of Hajj to include Ziyarat al-Nabi as a duty of state. It highlights the fiscal responsibility of the Islamic state to ensure inclusivity in worship by covering costs from the Bayt al-Mal for those lacking means, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the leader's role in facilitating religious practice. This ruling is often cited in discussions regarding the scope of 'compulsion' (ikrah) in non-mandatory acts when viewed through the lens of communal duty.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Bakhtary, and Hisham Bin Salim, and Muawiya Bin Ammar, and others, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If the people neglect the Hajj, it would be upon the governor that he compels them upon that, and upon the staying with it; and if they were to neglect the visitation of the Prophet<sup>saw</sup> (the Holy Shrine in Medina) it would be upon the governor that he compels them upon that, and upon the staying with it. So if they do not happen to have the wealth for them, he should spend from the Public Treasury of the Muslims’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs af-Bakhtariy and Hisham ibn Salim and Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar and others who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

if people neglect performing al-Hajj, the authorities will force them to perform al-Hajj and to reside therein. If people neglect visiting the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, the authorities will force them to do so and reside there. If they will not be able to bear the expenses, the authorities will pay for them from the public treasury.”
